idea_name: Polynomial regression std-dev channel as directed forecast regime
mechanism: From a preprocessed reference extremum, fit polynomial regression on OHLC series, extrapolate the central curve, and wrap ±k standard-deviation bands plus dynamic Stop levels from price deviation since the reference point; trade as a directed nonlinear channel whose slope/width encode local trend regime and forecast path.
data_needed: OHLC bar history (volumes ignored); reference/start extremum from fractal preprocessor; polynomial degree and lookback
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD examples; method stated for any TF M1–MN1
why_new_for_mis: Supplies MIS a nonlinear channel sensor (path + band width + predicted stops) richer than linear regression or MA envelopes for local trend-regime state.
quote: Data presentation for this purpose has to be based on the polynomial regression, where the extrapolated numerical series will be the target forecast

idea_name: Four primitive three-extrema fractals as trend/correction state machine
mechanism: Detect four primitive fractals from consecutive extrema A-B-C by relative height rules (uptrend, downward correction, upward correction, downtrend). Confirmation = price breaking beyond B; rules force confirmed uptrend→down correction and confirmed downtrend→up correction. Emits discrete regime-change labels on every TF.
data_needed: Swing/extrema series on the working TF; confirmation break of point B
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Any TF M1–MN1; EURUSD fractal examples including 2006–2008 structure
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a minimal discrete state sensor of trend vs correction transitions that is TF-agnostic and rule-closed (no oscillator lag).
quote: Any price movement on any time frame in the near future is explicitly determined by one of the four existing primitive fractals.

mechanism: Model each TF as three equilibrium cash flows (main river + two arms) whose banks are wave-regression channels; a fundamental/global flow bounds all junior fractals. Inflow/outflow imbalances drive price north/south; truncated vs extended trends classify flow exhaustion. Sense topology of nested liquidity regimes rather than single-series indicators.
data_needed: Multi-TF OHLC; fractal-wave matrix classifying stable fractals; wave-regression channel fits per flow
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD long/short flows; M1–MN1 nested fractals
why_new_for_mis: Frames liquidity as nested inertial cash-flow channels with explicit junior/senior coupling—usable as a multi-scale market-topology sensor for MIS.
quote: A developing fractal structure on every time frame forms equilibrium cash flows that remain stable for a certain time.

idea_name: Short-TF fractal destruction by market-noise limit
mechanism: Assert that identical fractal types should self-similarly scale from MN to ticks, but chaotic 'market noise' intensifies on shorter TFs; past a noise-level limit the fractal structure breaks and drops out of the stable matrix while price still obeys the senior fractal. Flag short-TF structure validity vs senior-flow dominance as a noise/volatility regime sensor.
data_needed: Fractal classifications across nested TFs; proxy for local noise intensity vs structure integrity
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Generic FX; contrast short TF vs longer TF stability
why_new_for_mis: Provides an explicit multi-scale validity gate: when junior fractal sensors fail, MIS should defer to senior-flow state instead of trusting broken short-TF patterns.
quote: When the market noise level exceeds a certain limit, the fractal structure breaks down.

idea_name: Joint-quote fractal dimension as FX coupling/independence sensor
mechanism: Embed N currency series as points in R^N; estimate fractal dimension D via Grassberger–Procaccia C(ε). Independent series fill available dimensions (D≈N); coupled series collapse toward a lower-D manifold. Apply to raw closes and to increments over M5–D1; rising D as pairs are added diagnoses residual free variables / weak coupling.
data_needed: Synchronized close (then increment) series for chosen FX basket; MATLAB/C frac estimators (box-counting or Grassberger–Procaccia)
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD, USDJPY, GBPUSD, AUDUSD, USDCHF, USDCAD, NZDUSD; M5, M15, M30, H1, H4, D1; 2000–2009
why_new_for_mis: Turns cross-pair dependence into a single scalar manifold-dimension sensor MIS can track for basket regime (coupled vs noise-filled independence).
quote: If currencies are interrelated, the fractal dimension, every time the new currency pair is added, should increase less and less significantly to finally get to a certain value that will determine the number of 'free variables' in the currency exchange market.

idea_name: Scale-break in C(ε) slope as noise-versus-structure threshold
mechanism: Plot log C(ε) vs log ε for an embedded set; locate the kink where slope jumps (e.g. ~1.0 on large scales to ~2.6 on small scales). The break ε* estimates the noise-tube diameter below which relationships vanish into uniform fill—use as a volatility/noise-scale sensor separating structured coupling from random walk.
data_needed: Point cloud from joint quotes or increments; C(ε) correlation-integral curve across ε grid
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Synthetic 3D noisy line validation; FX increment sets M5–D1 as in study
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a data-driven noise floor: below ε* treat cross-asset structure as unreliable; above it trust coupling/regime readings.
quote: An increase in fractal dimension at smaller scales allows to estimate a dimension at which the relationships between variables become indiscernible due to the presence of random noise.
